title: Closed models [notes postérieures à PS ?] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is notational bookkeeping for the universal properties of presheaf and copresheaf categories, and how they behave under passing to opposite categories.

Notation (read from context):
- A^ = Fun(A°, Set) is the category of presheaves on A.
- A^∨ := (A°)^ = Fun(A, Set) is the category of copresheaves.
- Hom_!(X, M) is the category of functors X → M that commute with colimits (inductive limits). The marginal gloss '! = ...' presumably explains this.
- Hom^!(X, M) is the category of functors X → M that commute with limits (projective limits).
- The annotation under M (read as 'stable fibr', perhaps 'stable par lim ind') means that M is assumed cocomplete.

Line 1: Hom(A, M) ≃ Hom_!(A^, M) for M cocomplete. This is the free-cocompletion property of the presheaf category. Restriction along the Yoneda embedding is an equivalence; its inverse is left Kan extension.

Line 2: Apply line 1 to A°:
- Hom(A°, M) ≃ Hom_!(A°^, M).
- Dualizing all categories gives (Hom^!(A°^°, M°))°.
- Here A°^° = A^∨° = Fun(A, Set)°. This is the free completion of A.
- The marginal note seems to record the dual hypothesis (completeness / 'stable' under the other kind of limits).

Line 3: Applying line 1 to M° (now assuming M complete):
- Hom(A, M°)° ≃ (Hom_!(A^, M°))° = Hom^!(A^°, M).
- Its left side Hom(A, M°)° is just Hom(A°, M), so it is joined to line 2 by the vertical ≃.

Struck-out box: an erroneous mixed formula Hom^!(A^∨, M°) ≃ Hom^!_!(A^, M°), which was discarded.

Corrected version: Hom_!(A^∨, M)° ≃ Hom_!(A^, M°). Both sides are identified with Hom(A°, M)°, which equals Hom(A, M°).

Last two lines restate the result cleanly:
- Hom(A°, M) ≃ Hom_!(A°^, M) = Hom_!(A^∨, M).
- Dually, Hom(A, M°) ≃ Hom_!(A^, M°).

Purpose: in this set of notes (closed models / derivators, after Pursuing Stacks), the previous page treats internal Hom and external products ⊠ in A^ × B^. The next page turns to filtered colimits in Hot. This page fixes the variance conventions for free (co)completions so they can be used for coefficient categories M (e.g. values of a derivator, assumed cocomplete and/or complete).

The lower half of the sheet is recycled computer paper: an IBM JCL job listing for MODULEF / FORTRAN compile-link steps, crossed out. It is unrelated to the mathematics.
errors: The boxed formula Hom^!(A^∨, M°) ≃ Hom^!_!(A^, M°) is wrong or ill-typed as written; Grothendieck himself struck it out and replaced it with Hom_!(A^∨, M)° ≃ Hom_!(A^, M°).

Hypotheses are implicit. Line 1 needs M cocomplete. The 'dual' lines need M complete (M° cocomplete). The chain of isomorphisms through Hom(A, M°)° therefore uses both properties at once; this is only hinted at by the marginal annotations.
Using the same symbol M and underlined M for categories versus objects is loose, but harmless.

ideas.what: Presheaf category A^ is the free cocompletion of A: colimit-preserving functors A^ → M correspond to functors A → M for M cocomplete.
ideas.modern_name: Universal property of the Yoneda embedding / free cocompletion (left Kan extension)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kan (1958); in topos form Grothendieck–Verdier SGA4 Exp. I
ideas.where_published: SGA4 Exp. I (extension of functors to presheaves); also used throughout Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs

ideas.what: Dual statement: Fun(A, Set)° is the free completion of A, and Hom^! (limit-preserving functors) arises by passing to opposite categories.
ideas.modern_name: Free completion via copresheaves; duality Hom_!(X, M) = Hom^!(X°, M°)°
ideas.where_published: Variance conventions of this kind appear in Les Dérivateurs, but not necessarily in this exact form

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine variance bookkeeping for free (co)completions, with one self-corrected error. It contains nothing beyond standard category theory.
transcription_corrections: The gloss after '! =' is largely illegible. It most plausibly abbreviates 'commutant aux lim inductives' (colimit-preserving), not a mathematical formula.
The annotation under M on line 1 is probably 'stable par lim' (i.e. cocomplete) rather than 'stable fibr'.
The marginal note on line 2 near M° is hard to read and may express the completeness hypothesis ('stable par lim proj' / similar). The reading 'cofibr' is doubtful.
The handwritten text rotated along the right margin ('(0, NE, COMP.FORT), EVEN') belongs to the JCL corrections, not to the mathematics.
In the boxed struck line, the second Hom carries both a superscript and a subscript '!'. The box is crossed out as a whole.
